messages:
morgan: FYI rolled the 'packlet affinity' change to canary at 22:03 PDT. Seeing a p99 jump ~120ms and sustained throughput drop ~8% on the canary cluster. Not huge but reproducible.
adhira: ack. Which part of the heuristic changed? packlet affinity was supposed to prefer same-kernel packing to reduce kernel switches, right?
morgan: yeah we started grouping by (kernel_id, seq_bucket) more aggressively and increased token_budget_target from 256 -> 384 for medium requests.
sam: can you paste the exact flag/config?
morgan: sure: ```continuous_batcher: { packlet_affinity: enabled, affinity_strength: 0.8, token_budget_target: 384, queue_smoothing_ms: 6 }```
ryan: quick question: did the kernel selection fallback frequency change? our perf counters show more 'kernel_flip' events on canary.
morgan: logs show kernel_router picked alternate kernels ~12% more often after the change. snippet from canary: "kernel_choose: primary=cu_fused_fp16, fallback=cu_fused_int8, chosen=fallback" repeated a lot.
adhira: hmm that suggests packlet grouping may have increased heterogeneity within a batch causing kernel mismatch and runtime fallback. Fallbacks are expensive + recompile penalties.
kevin: adding some profiler traces from a single failing pod: ```[PROFILE] batch_id=9523 shape=1x2048 tokens total=18 kernels: primary=cu_fused_fp16 attempts=3 fallback=cu_fallback_int8 time_ms=34->98```
qa-ci-bot: perf-regression alert: canary-p99 increased from 290ms -> 410ms for medium text-gen (window=1h).
sam: did we also change KV cache priming? packlet affinity might delay prefetch ordering so KV hits go down. KV hitrate drop would explain token inflation.
morgan: KV metrics: hitrate_medium before: 0.87 after: 0.78. miss latencies up ~10ms.
ryan: that aligns: more KV misses -> higher effective token cost and more kernel decisions mid-batch.
adhira: possible fixes: 1) lower affinity_strength to 0.4, 2) reduce token_budget_target back to 256, 3) add kernel-homogeneity check before sealing a packlet.
kevin: test quick simulation? I can run local microbench with synthetic arrivals and the new affinity to see where heterogeneity spikes.
morgan: running a rollback to affinity_strength=0.3 on canary now to isolate. Will keep token_budget at 384 for the experiment.
(10m later)
morgan: rolled affinity -> 0.3. p99 dropped ~70ms but still +50ms vs pre-change. throughput recovered ~4%.
sam: ok so affinity was big contributor but not whole story. Next suspect = token_budget_target. If it's larger we might wait longer to seal batches which increases chance of mixing shapes.
adhira: agree. Smaller token_budget -> more frequent seals -> less time mixing jobs of different kernel needs. Suggest revert token_budget_target to 256 on canary for A/B.
morgan: filed quick canary patch for token_budget_target=256, will monitor.
kevin: I'll push a stress run with KV prefetch enabled and disabled to see sensitivity.
ryan: long-term thought: we should include a kernel-homogeneity score in batch scoring to ensure packlet affinity doesn't sacrifice kernel locality for token packing. maybe weight = alpha * homogeneity + beta * token_util.
sam: +1. Also add canary probes to detect kernel_fallback rate spike and auto-shed affinity if fallback_rate > 5% in 2m window.
morgan: good suggestions. For immediate mitigation: revert token_budget and lower affinity_strength. If both look stable for 30m, will promote to stable.
adhira: please add an eval that runs sample traces and outputs expected kernel distribution so we catch regressions in CI.
morgan: noted. I'll create a follow-up thread with the perf graphs and canary pod IDs. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
